questions.solution:
**From the information given:**

A denotes ‘+’, B denotes ‘×’, C denotes ‘−’ and D denotes ‘÷’

We substitute the values in the given equation and solve it using BODMAS rule:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/13bc0065c96e715682af7c8a6dc1b4c567b7a2a89597cc68809a5ff942c7e421.png]

⇒ 92 + (__**121 ÷ 11**__) - (__**6 × 3**__) ÷ 2 + 7 × 8 = ?

⇒ 92 + 11 - __**18 ÷ 2**__ + 7 × 8 = ?

⇒ 92 + 11 - 9 + __**7 × 8**__ = ? 

⇒ __**92 + 11**__ - 9 __**+ 56**__ = ?

⇒ __**159 - 9**__ = ?

⇒ **150 = Answer**

Hence **the correct answer is option 1)**

questions.question: Seven friends P, Q, R, S, T, U and V, each has got different marks in the board examination. P scored higher than only U and R. R scored higher than U. Q scored higher than S but lesser than T. T has not scored the highest among all. How many persons scored between Q and R?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

1) P scored higher than **only** U and R ⇒ **P** > U and R 

2) R scored higher than U ⇒ **R **> U

3) Q scored higher than S but lesser than T ⇒ T > **Q** > S

5) T has not scored the highest among all

So, the correct order will be ⇒ V > T > Q > S > P > R > U 

So, there are two persons who scored between Q and R.

Hence, the option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number-pairs EXCEPT one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.solution:
**LOGIC : Square root of first number + 3 = Second number**

Lets check each option: 

1) 81 ∶ 12 ⇒ √81 + 3 = 9 + 3 = 12

2) 64 ∶ 11 ⇒ √64 + 3 = 8 + 3 = 11

3) 100 ∶ 13 ⇒ √100 + 3 = 10 + 3 = 13

4) 121 ∶ 16 ⇒ √121 + 3 = 11 + 3 = **14 ≠ 16**

Hence, **"121 ∶ 16"** is the odd one out.

questions.question:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some pots are boxes.

All stands are boxes.

Some cartons are stands.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some cartons are boxes.

II. Some cartons are pots.

III. Some pots are stands.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow

questions.solution:
**Statements:**

Some pots are boxes.

All stands are boxes.

Some cartons are stands.

**Possible Venn diagram:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d36fa703ce6540c3ddcd3accae0690248f0229404de1313980428a6e183a88ea.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. Some cartons are boxes →** True** (Since some cartons are stands and all stands are boxes)

II. Some cartons are pots → False (It may be possible but not definite)

III. Some pots are stands → False (It may be possible but not definite)

Hence, **only conclusion 1 follows.**
